svg.title: Lien and Fraud Gates Before the Iron Moves
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-lien-and-fraud-gates; chapter number: 5; title: Lien and Fraud Gates Before the Iron Moves; subtitle: Prove the machine is not already pledged, then prove the money; chart type: decision_tree; nodes: gate: G1; question: Does a Secretary of State UCC search on the debtor's exact legal name come back clean?; pass next: G2; fail action: Order the $15 Texas plain copy to read the collateral description; have the dealer pay the lender directly, as in $8,000 to the lender and $2,000 to the seller on $10,000.; gate: G2; question: Does a separate search under the secured party's name clear blanket liens?; pass next: G3; fail action: Never clear collateral on a UCC-3 termination alone; verify the underlying debt is satisfied.; gate: G3; question: Does the hull, motor, trailer, or machine carry a readable serial, HIN, or VIN?; pass next: G4; fail action: Walk away; it could be stolen product.; gate: G4; question: Is payment a verified wire, with no cashier's check and no stand-in collector for an out-of-state buyer?; pass next: Release the machine; fail action: Stop the release; verify any changed wiring instructions by calling a number already held, never one from the email.; caption: A buyer who takes a liened machine can lose it to the original lender; a misspelled debtor name can hide a million-dollar lien.; assumptions note: UCC filings generally stay active for five years. New York search fee is $25 by credit card; copies require check or money order. Gate order assembled from separate practitioner rules.; note: Sources - Garden Shop Pro, NerdWallet Small Business, CSC, OnWaterTVAustralia, Boom & Bucket, Living in Fort Myers, and jesseleblancatlanta.

text.title: Lien and Fraud Gates Before the Iron Moves
text.tspan: Lien and Fraud Gates Before the Iron Moves

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Does a Secretary of State UCC search on the debtor's exact legal name come back clean?; pass next: G2; fail action: Order the $15 Texas plain copy to read the collateral description; have the dealer pay the lender directly, as in $8,000 to the lender and $2,000 to the seller on $10,000.

gate: G2; question: Does a separate search under the secured party's name clear blanket liens?; pass next: G3; fail action: Never clear collateral on a UCC-3 termination alone; verify the underlying debt is satisfied.
gate: G3; question: Does the hull, motor, trailer, or machine carry a readable serial, HIN, or VIN?; pass next: G4; fail action: Walk away; it could be stolen product.

gate: G4; question: Is payment a verified wire, with no cashier's check and no stand-in collector for an out-of-state buyer?; pass next: Release the machine; fail action: Stop the release; verify any changed wiring instructions by calling a number already held, never one from the email.

text.title: Assumptions: UCC filings generally stay active for five years. New York search fee is $25 by credit card; copies require check or money order. Gate order assembled from separate practitioner rules.
text.tspan: Assumptions: UCC filings generally stay active for five years. New York search fee is $25 by credit card; copies require check or
money order. Gate order assembled from separate practitioner rules.
